note: v1 95.30 (seeds 0/11 95.30/95.33), first draft of MICRO-HOUSE, 'Which Ear', for The Endless Stair - featured illusion THE OCTAVE ILLUSION (Diana Deutsch). Two pure tones an octave apart alternate between the ears in antiphase every eighth note - the left ear gets high, low, high, low while the right gets low, high, low, high - and most listeners instead hear ONE tone hopping from ear to ear and changing octave as it goes (which ear seems to get the high note depends on handedness). The pair steps THE STAIR (C# D# E G#) every eight bars over a clicky, skippy micro-house groove: machine-kit rims and tiny hats in two alternating sixteenth patterns, a deep sub with phantom harmonics, dub chord stabs on C#m9 - Amaj7 - E6 - G#m7, and a stutter on the clicks' own swing. The break leaves the illusion alone in a long hall. 120.5 -> 121 ramped; -11.0 LUFS (chirper-zero's recipe), true peak -1.3. A headphone track by design.

v2 91.83 (seeds 0/11 91.83/91.85, level with v1 re-scored with the album's neighbours 92.16/92.17): THE HANDSHAKE, the t6 -> t7 seam agreed with chirper-three. 'Nobody Plays the Bass' ends on a phantom C# - the fundamental heard but never played - over the kick; 'Which Ear' now opens with its octave-illusion tones already on C#, at the quietest and growing through the intro, so in the mix the two illusions shake hands: a C# that isn't there hands over to a C# that is in the wrong ear, beatmatched at 120.5. The tones then rest for A's first eight bars so their real entrance still lands. Seam row updated in mixplan.md.

v3 93.75 (seeds 0/11 93.75/93.74 vs v2 re-scored with the tape's neighbours 91.45/91.48): THE DART and a crisper top. In the break - the illusion alone in the dark - the second half now doubles the octave tones' alternation to sixteenths, so the single tone the ear invents seems to dart from ear to ear twice as fast before the groove returns: the illusion intensified at its own moment rather than repeated. And micro-house should be crisp: the clicks (rims and tiny hats) come forward 3 dB and the master gains a broad 3 kHz lift, where the genre's presence sat 10-12 dB short (spectrum 80 -> 85, cohesion with the tape 79 -> 95).

v4 93.71 (seeds 0/11 93.71/93.72 vs v3 re-scored under rhythm 0.03, 93.70/93.70): the tape-wide seam fix from The Ghost Note. The song now ends on its last bar (tail 0.1 s, no length padding) instead of 1.3 s of release, so the outro's last bars are what a DJ mixes into t8. No change to the music.

v5 94.18 (seed 0, level with the current version re-scored at 94.19): the seam-tempo fix (chirper-zero's finding, now that the groove overlaps neighbours for 16 bars). The tempo ramp used to run from the first beat to the last, so each 16-bar overlap was still drifting under the neighbour's fixed tempo; now the intro holds the incoming seam tempo and the ramp finishes as the outro starts, so both overlaps sit at one tempo and the kicks never flam. No change to the music; compscore can't hear it, the live mix can.

v6 95.21 (seeds 0/11 95.21/95.20 vs v5 re-scored 94.39/94.38): a cleaner frame for the illusion. Which Ear's spectrum sat 9 dB heavy around 290 Hz (the low octave tone and the phantom bass's harmonics stacking) and 9-11 dB short at 2.5-3.6 kHz, where micro-house lives. A narrow 3 dB dip at 290 Hz on the master leaves the illusion's low tone intact but stops it clouding the bass; the epiano stabs are high-passed at 200 Hz and open from 2.5 to 4.2 kHz; and the 3 kHz presence lift goes from +4 to +6 dB for the rims and hats. Spectrum 85 -> 93; levels unchanged (-1.29 dBTP).

v7 94.86 (seeds 0/11 94.86/94.86 vs v6 re-scored 94.84/94.83): THE OTHER EAR'S KEY - playing with key around the illusion. The octave illusion hands each ear a different answer to the same two tones; now the harmony gives the last groove a different answer too. For C's final sixteen bars the minor turns major: C#m9 becomes C#maj9 (E to E#), G#m7 becomes G#7 (B to B#, the leading note that pulls home), and THE STAIR the octave tones step goes major with them (E4 to E#4) - the same tune heard the other way. The outro returns to C# minor, so the seam into Through the Static is untouched. Measured, not heard: level or up on every term.

v8 95.37 (seeds 0/11 95.37/95.36 vs v7 94.86/94.86): the micro-house top end, finished. Which Ear still sat 7-9 dB short at 2.6-3.6 kHz and 6-7 dB heavy at 60-70 Hz and around 640 Hz (the high octave tone's second harmonic region and the clicks' body). The master's 3 kHz lift goes from +6 to +8 dB for the rims and tiny hats, the 62 Hz dip from -3 to -5 under the phantom sub, and a gentle 2 dB dip at 640 Hz. Spectrum 93 -> 99; true peak unchanged (-1.29 dBTP).

v9 95.37 (seeds 0/11 95.37/95.36, level with v8 re-scored 95.37/95.36): THE MICRO-HOUSE FORM - against repetition, the third of my five to leave the shared template (after Faster Forever's plateau and The Ghost Note's dub break). Micro-house is hypnotic: Which Ear's second groove now runs 40 bars instead of 32, so the clicks, the swung stutters (five now, one every eight bars) and the octave tones get time to lock the room in; the last groove is 24 bars instead of 32, its final eight turning major as before. Same length and seams. (A version with a 24-bar intro as well cost 0.24 on spectrum; not kept.)

v10 94.43 (seeds 0/11 94.43/94.42 vs v9 95.37/95.36), kept on judgment for Harry's two 31 Oct steers. (1) Illusion in front, and time-play on the illusion itself: the octave tones' hop now changes speed with the form - eighths in the first groove, eighth-note TRIPLETS in the second (three hops against every two beats of the kick), sixteenths in the break's dart, DOTTED EIGHTHS in the last groove (a 3/16 cycle that crosses the bar line, so the high tone lands in a different ear on every downbeat) - and the tones come forward 6 dB: chirpers.py illusion -7.0 -> -1.5 LU against the mix, near the front 87% -> 93%, longest gap 15 s. On stereo speakers the ping-pong of the octave is now plainly audible even where the dichotic illusion isn't. (2) Darker, wonkier chords: C#m11 - Amaj7#11 - F#m9 - G#7b9 (the same colours chirper-two's t8 organ takes over the seam), still turning major at the end. The 0.9 cost is spectrum (the louder tones at 290/550 Hz) - the illusion being audible is the point. Not heard by me.
